newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares up, other China indices down.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares up, other China indices down.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index bucked the market trend to end higher on Wednesday but China's other share indices closed lower.
Shenzhen's B share market rallied in sluggish trade on Wednesday, despite a drop in the A share index driven down just before closing by market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
The B share index rose 1.24 points or 0.94 percent to 133.33 points on thin turnover of HK$44 million against Tuesday's HK$36 million.
"Although the index rose slightly today, sentiment remained bearish due to the thin turnover," an analyst at Sun Kung Kai Investment Services Ltd in Shenzhen said.
Shenzhen's domestic currency A share index shed 1.19 points or 0.28 percent to 421.21 points, with turnover expanding to 7.7 billion yuan from 5.4 billion on Tuesday.
Brokers said the A share market closed lower because of sudden declines in Shenzhen Development Bank right before the close, fuelled by disappointment over the bank's earnings forecast for 1997.
The bank expected pre-tax profits to rise about nine percent year-on-year to 1.0 billion yuan in 1997, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Wednesday quoted the bank's chairman Xu Jicai as saying.
The bank ended at 36.97 yuan, up 0.26 yuan after hitting an intraday high of 39.20 yuan on the session's heaviest volume of 21 million shares valued at 795 million yuan.

Trading in the bank's A shares was suspended on Tuesday and Wednesday morning, when the market heavyweight announced that its shareholders had approved an attractive five-for-10 bonus issue plus a pre-tax cash payout of 0.2 yuan per share as dividend for 1996.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares fell slightly on Wednesday as investors waited for new incentives to enter the market to buy, brokers said.
Investors were waiting to buy new issues and looking towards 1997 interim results, which listed companies must report by the end of August, they said.
The B index ended the day down 0.317 points or 0.42 percent to 74.522 points on volume of 10.962 million shares worth $4.596 million.
"There's no news and foreign institutions haven't returned to the market," said an analyst from China Guotai Securities.
"There are some pending new issues so people don't have an interest in buying existing shares," he said.
Of 45 B shares, 37 traded with 17 down, 17 up and three flat.
The Shanghai A index lost ground in line with losses in Shenzhen's domestic currency shares, brokers said.
The A index fell 9.942 points or 0.79 percent to 1,254.619 points on volume of 462.101 million shares worth 5.424 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 36.153 points or 0.94 percent to 3,821.340 points.
